{{Short description|Formula for estimating hiking speed}}
[[File:Tobler's hiking function.svg|thumb|300px|Tobler's hiking function – walking speed vs. slope angle chart.]]
'''Tobler's hiking function''' is an [[exponential function]] determining the [[hiking]] speed, taking into account the [[Grade (slope)|slope]] angle.<ref name="Tobler93" /><ref name="Magyari12" /><ref name="Kondo10" /> It was formulated by [[Waldo Tobler]]. This function was estimated from empirical data of the Swiss cartography professor [[Eduard Imhof]].<ref name="Imhof50" />

==Formula==
Walking velocity:

: <math>W=6e^{\displaystyle-3.5\left\vert\frac{dh}{dx}+0.05\right\vert}</math>

: <math>\frac{dh}{dx}=S=\tan\theta</math>

where

: ''W'' = walking velocity [km/h]<ref name="Magyari12" />
: ''dh'' = elevation difference,
: ''dx'' = distance,
: ''S'' = slope,
: ''&theta;'' = angle of slope (inclination).

The velocity on the flat terrain is 5&nbsp;km / h, the maximum speed of 6&nbsp;km / h is achieved roughly at -2.86°.<ref name="Irtenkauf14" />

On flat terrain this formula works out to 5&nbsp;km/h. For off-path travel, this value should be multiplied by 3/5, for horseback by 5/4.<ref name="Tobler93" />

== Pace ==
[[Pace (running)|Pace]] is the reciprocal of speed.<ref name="Kay12_1" /><ref name="Kay12_2" /> For Tobler's hiking function it can be calculated from the following conversion:<ref name="Kay12_2" />

: <math>p=0.6e^{\displaystyle3.5\left\vert m+0.05\right\vert}</math>

where

: ''p'' = pace [s/m]
: ''m'' = gradient uphill or downhill (''dh/dx = S'' in Tobler's formula),
